title: Two styles: plunger and open horn
summary: The plunger was Bubber Miley's trademark that Cootie learned from Tricky Sam; his own open style came from Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Well, listen. Just while we're talking about that, the plunger, one time when you and I were doing an interview earlier, you started talking to me about the plunger. Well, first of all, last time we talked you laughed about it and said that it seemed like funny to you. But afterwards, you told me that that just became a part of you.

Yeah, it did become a part of me, because that was what Duke Ellington hired me to do. And it dawned on me. I had taken Bubber Miley's place, and that was Bubber Miley's trademark, the plunger. And I was almost a legit trumpet player at that time. I had just left Fletcher Henderson's band, playing first trumpet. And coming in -- and I never used a plunger. Then by, you know, sitting and listening to Joe Tricky Sam Nanton, that's how I picked it up.
Well, but the thing is this, you know. You were pointing out that you had like two ways of being yourself. You -- I mean, as you said, Louis was your idol. And so you used to blow open horn.
And you used to blow like Louis was your
inspiration. That was really the style, wasn't it. I mean, it was your interpretation of this -- that field.
That's right, isn't it, in a sense. So that was you and the you that used the plunger was another you altogether, because those two styles are -- well, they're totally different, aren't they?
